name: universal-provenance
description: Read, write, validate, verify, browse, and export a Universal Provenance Corpus (UPC) with byte-exact quotation gates.

tools.name: upc_validate
tools.description: Validate a UPC corpus against the spec/08 rule registry: schema conformance, referential integrity, content-addressed id recompute, and the hop-A/B/C quotation gates (byte-exact). Prints a bounded JSON report keyed by error code; level is computed from rules passed. Exits non-zero on any error.

tools.name: upc_verify_quotes
tools.description: Run the hop-C gate over any output file: every "…" [ext-id] marker must equal that extraction's direct_quote exactly. The gate for anything an LLM emits with quotations. Exits non-zero on any mismatch.

tools.name: upc_quote
tools.description: Print an exact, ready-to-paste citation marker "<quote>" [ext-id] for a verified extraction. --narrow mints a sub-quote extraction (deterministic slice) and prints its marker. The copy-don't-retype path.

tools.name: upc_verify
tools.description: Report the full verification chain (hop A rep-hash + hop B quote-gate) for one extraction, with a reanchor hint if the quote drifted.

tools.name: upc_locate
tools.description: Resolve every locator on an extraction into a structured context bundle: the verified span plus its surrounding text and derived line number, and each advisory presentation locator (page, region, timestamp) with its trust label. The API a reading surface calls to bring a quotation's source up in place. Read-only.

tools.name: upc_regen
tools.description: Regenerate corpus.json (counts, indexes, schema_hash), the CSV mirrors, and index.html from the objects, atomically. The projection-refresh and crash-recovery command.

tools.name: upc_export
tools.description: Export bibliographic and object projections: CSL-JSON (authoritative), BibTeX, RIS, JSONL (raw objects), a Markdown bibliography, a deterministic RO-Crate 1.3 metadata graph (--format ro-crate writes ro-crate-metadata.json into the corpus root; --copy -o <dir> emits a detached self-contained crate), or a deterministic W3C PROV-O derivation graph as flattened JSON-LD (--format prov, streamed to stdout or -o <file>). All exports are read-only projections; the UPC objects stay canonical, and the quotation gate is UPC-only (not carried into PROV). --format obsidian writes a readable Obsidian vault (-o <dir> standalone, or --into <vault> for an existing vault's inbox): one Markdown note per source, generation and synthesis, images copied into the attachment folder with their descriptions as folded captions, and each note's origin in a folded provenance callout. It is the one LOSSY export — navigation, running heads and page numbers are removed so the note is the content — and it reports what it stripped in each note; quotations are still rendered from the representation bytes at the locator and still carry their gate badge. It is byte-idempotent and will not overwrite a note edited by hand.

tools.name: upc_reanchor
tools.description: After a representation is re-rendered, byte-exact-search the successor for each affected quote: a unique match mints a replacement extraction (supersedes chain); zero or multiple matches flag needs_review. Never re-anchors silently.

tools.name: upc_build_index
tools.description: Generate a self-contained, offline index.html browser (a projection): findability, the provenance graph both ways, and a verification badge on every quotation with context read from the representation at the locator. Read-only, written atomically.

tools.name: upc_mint
tools.args_hint: [--batch] <src|rep|ext|gen|syn|cod|cbk>  (JSON object, or JSONL with --batch, on stdin)
tools.description: Compute a content-addressed id (spec/06 recipe) for an object read from stdin. Deterministic across implementations.

tools.name: upc_anchor
tools.description: Byte-exact-anchor candidate quotations proposed by a model. Each stdin line is {quote, type?, query?, note?}. A quote occurring EXACTLY ONCE in the representation mints an active char_range extraction that passes the hop-B gate by construction; zero or multiple occurrences return not_found/ambiguous and are never written as verified. The model chooses what to extract; this decides what is real. Writes only unique hits and journals one extract event.

tools.name: upc_code
tools.description: Batch-apply codings (spec/12). Each stdin line is {codebook_ref, code|value, target:{kind,id}, coder, confidence?, rationale?}. Validates each against its codebook (closed vs open, code membership, target resolution), mints the cod- id, supersedes any prior judgement by the same coder on the same target, and updates the set manifest. Re-running an unchanged pass writes nothing.

tools.name: upc_codebook
tools.description: List the coding schemes in a corpus, or inspect one: its codes, definitions, hierarchy, and how many times each code has actually been applied (computed, never stored). Read-only.

tools.name: upc_batch
tools.description: Run many read-only queries over ONE corpus load. Each stdin line is {cmd: locate|verify|quote|codebook, ...}; results stream back as NDJSON. Use this instead of invoking upc once per passage: locate is O(whole corpus) per call, so per-passage shelling out is quadratic.

tools.name: upc_version
tools.description: Report the spec version this build implements, the hash of its schema set, and the available commands. Pair with `upc check-compat --requires "^1.6"` (exit 1 on mismatch) so an embedding tool fails loudly on a version skew instead of drifting silently.

requires.schemas: UPC schemas/ and vocab/ (walk-up discovery, or UPC_SCHEMA_DIR / UPC_VOCAB_DIR)
